matches.stipulation: UPW World Heavyweight Championship Tournament first round
matches.notes: Williams hit three German suplexes and a second-rope knee drop before finishing with "Moment of Clarity" (a supernatural piledriver).
Shabazz pinned with "Hard Truth" (a spinning flapjack into the corner); Shabazz refused to let the referee raise his own hand in victory.
Ricky Courage pinned Grimmace with a bridging German suplex ("Sunplex"); Titan Juarez stood at ringside but did not wrestle.
Foley pinned with "Air Dublin" (a handspring cutter).
Lewis pinned with "Round Tripper" (a 450 splash).

Donegal had Keenan in the Wolf Trap ankle lock when Malcom Shabazz ran in and kicked Donegal in the head, drawing the disqualification. Shabazz then rampaged post-bell — chokeslamming Donegal, knocking manager Adam Lazarus off the apron, shoving the referee down, and press-slamming Keenan onto Lazarus outside the ring — before eight security officers restrained him.

While Wilson argued a rope-break ruling with the referee, Chambers rolled him up with a backslide for a surprise pin. Afterward a hooded run-in, revealed as Damian Payne, chokeslammed Chambers ("ChokeBomb") and left with Wilson.

matches.stipulation: UPW World Heavyweight Championship Tournament Advancement Match
matches.notes: Semi-main event. Williams reversed a De Luca right hand into a crucifix pin, advancing to the Fatal Four-Way for the vacant World Heavyweight Championship on 22 November 2016.

matches.stipulation: Best two-out-of-three falls; vacant UPW World Tag Team Championship
matches.notes: Main event. Fall 1 (Hype) by double-countout scramble; Fall 2 (Warriors) by Kel Robertson powerbomb on Danny Nash after manager Syn was ejected for striking DeAwn Carter; Fall 3 (Warriors, deciding) by Robertson's spike reverse piledriver "Justice" on Nash. First UPW World Tag Team Champions.

matches.notes: Manager Sammy Sharifi interfered for the Warriors; Titan Juarez — having previously walked out on Soldiers of the Sun — ran in and chokeslammed both Dominion members, drawing the disqualification. matches.stipulation: Survival Rumble entry-number stipulation: winner gets the #40/best slot, loser gets #1/worst
matches.notes: Malcom Shabazz and two "Hard Truth Soldiers" attempted interference; Cardinal invited Shabazz to hit him for a DQ win, and Shabazz refused. An earlier fast-counted pin was overturned for Donegal's own foot on the rope before Cardinal's "LD50" won it clean, taking the #40 slot to Donegal's #1. Shabazz attacked the fallen Donegal before security removed him; Cardinal's own sit-down chair promo demanding a title shot back from management drew out Glenn Chambers, and the two brawled from the ring through the backstage area and concourse, ending with Chambers powerbombing Cardinal ("Locked and Loaded") through a merchandise table — "that was for DJ."

matches.stipulation: Number One Contender's Match for the UPW World Heavyweight Championship at Survival; John Herdick as special guest referee; main event
matches.notes: Two additional unnamed referees were stationed at ringside per Aaron Lewis's own request for fairness. Herdick appeared to turn on Rage — knocking him out from behind with brass knuckles and shaking hands with Styles in an apparent fix — but Jeff Keenan ran in and hit both Herdick and Styles with a "Quickstryke," foiling the screwjob; Rage recovered, hit "Hammer of God" on Styles, and an unnamed regular referee made the count. Rage earns the World Title shot against Aaron Lewis at Survival.

matches.notes: Billed as Gaines vs. Caleb Foley, but Foley was found beaten and bleeding backstage before the show (an unexplained assault the broadcast opens on); Gaines was initially awarded a forfeit win before Chase Williams emerged from the back and the bell was rung for a substitute match instead. Williams squashed Gaines with a running clothesline, a snapmare DDT, and a legsweep STO into the turnbuckle before setting up a powerbomb the referee stopped the match rather than let land — a crowd "Foley" chant afterward, and Williams's own smirking non-denial, imply Williams was behind the backstage assault.

Billy James's own "Thirty Eight Special" DDT won a back-and-forth match by pinfall. Afterward, an enraged Skylark attacked the referee, sprint-tackled James on the ramp, locked in "Choking the Chicken" until security intervened, then beat James bloody with a steel chair — the first sign of the darker persona Skylark carries into UPW's own final broadcast.
Brody won convincingly, then tossed Love Machine over the top rope twice more for good measure as the crowd booed.
